correctness.rationale: The local leaf rule proves each pair costs at least 2 and (0,2) is the sole weight-2 type; core vertices at cost≥3 dominate G, implying weight≥2n+gamma. Equality forces exact cost-3 types; the outside-D adjacency criterion and the single excluded globally nonmaximal labeling give a genuine bijection. The cyclic gap-deficit proof covers n=3, n=4 and all residues; brute-force original-definition checks on 80 base graphs and separate cycle checks corroborate it.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Corollary 3(i) of Cariaga–Jamil implies the 2n+gamma(G) value (for connected nontrivial G), because maximizing |V0| of an ordinary DRDF gives n−gamma(G). The theorem claims no novelty for that value. The classification of every optimal maximal function as the stated (D,S) pair types, counting factor 2^gamma−1, and exact 3-residue sunlet counts do not follow from those scalar statements without new local equality reasoning.

value.rationale: A natural equality-case classification for maximal double Roman domination on a full graph product family, resolving counts of all optimizer functions rather than repeating known minimum values. The pair-indexed structure (minimum D, eligible S, 2^gamma−1 choices) and mod-three sunlet enumeration have substantive combinatorial content, including n=4 count 30 and distinct gap types; no general downstream theorem is claimed as necessary.
